Don’t Chase the Zone. Build the Rhythm First――集中の入口は「次が読める時間」にある

Maybe the route into the zone is not “concentrate harder,” but “build a rhythm first.” Flow research points to clear goals, immediate feedback, and challenge-skill balance as key antecedents, while qualitative work suggests a preparation phase before flow entry. Rhythm research shows that regular timing can create temporal expectation—an advance sense of when the next event will occur. But music is not automatically helpful: lyrics can disrupt reading and memory. This essay reframes rhythm not as background music but as a predictable action-feedback cycle: one move, one response, the next move.
